title: EvidenceProjection — 证据账本投影的读回信封（GET /api/evidence-projection）
description: What a person is allowed to conclude about the evidence link of the chain. Every number and token here is recomputed by src/design_lab/governance/evidence_readback.py from design-lab/config/task-ledger-r3.json plus the object database -- never read out of reports/current/, which is a generated projection that binds whatever commit it was written at. Two separate questions are kept separate because conflating them made every receipt unverifiable on 2026-10-08: `verified` asks whether the bytes a receipt hashed are still where the receipt says they came from, `current` asks whether that receipt still describes the bytes this service is running. The reason lists are closed enums: a new reason token in the code without a registration here is a contract violation, so the vocabulary a reader sees cannot drift from the vocabulary the projection emits. An empty `receipts` list means the ledger has no records; it never means 'the evidence is fine', which is why totals are required alongside it.

subjectSha.description: The commit this readback was computed against. A receipt's own subjectSha may be an ancestor; that is what `current` distinguishes.

ledger.description: Repository-relative path of the ledger the receipts were read from, so a reader knows which record set the numbers describe.

outcomePass.description: Receipts whose outcome is PASS. A PARTIAL or FAIL receipt is honest history and is never counted as verified evidence.

current.description: Subset of `verified` whose claimed bytes still equal the bytes at subjectSha.

taskCounts.description: Projected task status counts, so a reader cannot be shown evidence strength without the acceptance state it belongs to.

integrityReason.description: Why the receipt's own byte claims no longer reproduce where the receipt says they came from.

currencyReason.description: Why an intact receipt is not evidence about the bytes this service is running.
